subject: physics
question_text: Does the escape velocity of a body depend on its mass or on the direction of projection? Give the reason.

steps.label: The mass

steps.why: The heavier body needs more energy, but it also has more energy at the same speed — the two effects cancel exactly.
common_mistakes: Saying a heavier body needs a larger escape velocity.

recall.must_convey: That the mass cancels in the escape condition, so v e does not depend on m.
accept: v e is root 2 g R with no m
reject: kinetic energy depends only on the size of the velocity

steps.memory_tip: The m sits on BOTH sides of ½mv² = GMm/R, so it cancels and cannot matter.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Answer no first, then show the m cancelling.

lines.text: v_e depends only on M and R of the planet

steps.why: The one practical exception is a direction that sends the body back into the ground; for any projection clear of the surface the direction makes no difference.
common_mistakes: Saying a vertical projection needs a smaller escape velocity than a slanting one.

recall.must_convey: That kinetic energy depends only on the size of the velocity, so the direction does not matter.
accept: kinetic energy depends only on the speed

steps.memory_tip: Kinetic energy is ½mv², and v² holds no direction. Straight up or slanting, the same speed.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name energy as the reason; direction is not in ½mv².

insider_note: Two questions, a mark each, and each needs its own reason — m cancelling, and energy depending only on speed.
